channel.title: From the blog
channel.description: Learnings, recommendations & new features from ServiceStack engineers

item.title: Build a Redis Streams Work Queue in C# That Survives Worker Crashes
item.author: demis@servicestack.com (Demis)
item.description: ServiceStack.Redis v10.5 adds Redis Streams with typed entries, consumer groups, explicit acknowledgments and recovery of a crashed worker's messages, then keeps your workers within your Redis plan with an opt-in cap on pool connections, bounded and cancellable waits and fully async connection setup

item.title: Redis Caching in .NET with IDistributedCache, HybridCache and Atomic TTLs
item.author: demis@servicestack.com (Demis)
item.description: ServiceStack.Redis v10.5 puts your Redis behind ASP.NET Core's IDistributedCache and HybridCache, writes every value and its expiry in one atomic step, and adds the Redis commands for expiring exactly what you mean, from a one-time token to a single field in a hash

item.title: Astro + .NET for Content Sites That Ship No JavaScript by Default
item.author: demis@servicestack.com (Demis)
item.description: ServiceStack v10.5 adds an astro-static template for blogs, docs, marketing and product sites that still need auth and .NET APIs, with pages that are plain HTML, React islands only where you need them, a typed Markdown and MDX blog validated at build time, all served by your .NET App

item.title: TanStack Start + .NET with Type-safe Routes and No Node.js Server
item.author: demis@servicestack.com (Demis)
item.description: ServiceStack v10.5 adds a tanstack-static template where every link and route param is type checked, every page is prerendered for fast first loads then runs as a SPA, and dynamic routes don't need to be known at build time, all served by your .NET App with no Node.js server to run in production

item.title: React, Next.js and Vue Templates Upgraded to Vite+
item.author: demis@servicestack.com (Demis)
item.description: ServiceStack v10.5 moves every React, Next.js and Vue template to Vite+, replacing a stack of separate tools and config files with one vp CLI and one vite.config.ts that formats, lints, type checks, tests and builds your front-end, with the same rules in your editor, in CI and for your AI Agent

item.title: Why Is My .NET App Slow? Find and Fix Slow SQL From Your Browser
item.author: demis@servicestack.com (Demis)
item.description: ServiceStack v10.4 adds db.Explain() to OrmLite to return the query plan of any typed query from C#, and a Slowest Queries view to the Profiling Admin UI where you can explain, analyze and re-run your App's slowest queries from the browser

item.title: Resilient Retries and Read Replicas in OrmLite
item.author: demis@servicestack.com (Demis)
item.description: ServiceStack v10.4 lets OrmLite safely retry deadlocks, throttling and failovers from one line of configuration, and spread reads over a read replica whose read-only connections catch the classic replica bug in development instead of in production

item.title: Vector search in OrmLite
item.author: demis@servicestack.com (Demis)
item.description: ServiceStack v10.4 adds first-class [Vector] columns to OrmLite, so the embeddings of an AI model are stored with your data and the rows most similar to a question are found in the same typed query as your filters, joins and tenant rules, on PostgreSQL, SQL Server, MariaDB, MySQL and SQLite

item.title: Query JSON like any other property in OrmLite
item.author: demis@servicestack.com (Demis)
item.description: ServiceStack v10.4 lets typed OrmLite queries read straight into complex type properties with x.Address.City or x.Lines.Any(...), using the native JSON functions of SQLite, PostgreSQL, SQL Server and MySQL, plus a complete tour of everything else OrmLite can do with JSON

item.title: Advanced SQL queries in typed OrmLite
item.author: demis@servicestack.com (Demis)
item.description: ServiceStack v10.4 adds typed recursive queries, named sub queries, window functions with TopPerGroup, Union/Intersect/Except, SeekAfter keyset paging and async streaming, so the queries that used to need hand-written SQL stay typed, parameterized and portable
